text: The council voted to approve the vacation of the portion of Maple Way between Long Beach Boulevard and Alamo Court District to accommodate a development project.
Public Works Department will proceed with the vacation of the alley as approved.
No specific risks were mentioned in the transcript.
No open questions were raised during the meeting.

The motion to increase appropriations in the general fund group and the Economic Development Department by $25,000 to support the creation of a community vision for business corridor improvements on historic Pine Avenue and the North Pine Neighborhood was approved.
Councilwoman Gonzales will present the recommendation following her arrival from a graduation event.
The motion to request the city manager to provide an update on Laura's Law within 60 days was carried.
The city manager is tasked with providing an update on Laura's Law within 60 days.
Councilmembers are to receive and review the report on Laura's Law, with a focus on patient rights and the L.A. County pilot program.
There is a risk of misunderstanding or misrepresentation of patient rights and the implications of Laura's Law.
There is a risk of criminalizing individuals with mental health issues, which is opposed by several advocacy groups.
How is the L.A. County pilot program addressing patient rights and the balance between public safety and individual freedoms?
What are the alternative approaches to supporting individuals with mental health issues, and how can the city incentivize access to support services?

The Council recommended to award contracts to Corbin and C.J. Concrete Construction for the construction of curb ramps and concrete-related improvements, with a total amount not to exceed $30 million citywide.
Public Works is to provide documentation regarding any wage compliance issues with C.J. Construction, including any findings from other jurisdictions, in a 'two from four' format.

The council approved the motion to finalize and execute a master license agreement with Verizon Communications for the nonexclusive use of city-owned properties for wireless telecommunications facilities citywide.
The city staff and Verizon will continue working on the rollout and next steps of the agreement.
The motion to require the city attorney to draft an ordinance amending the Long Beach Municipal Code to add hotel worker safety provisions was approved.
City attorney's office to draft the ordinance with the added hotel worker safety provisions.
